metadata.title: US Senate fails to pass war powers resolution to limit Trump's use of military force in Iran

left: The US Senate voted 53-47 against a war powers resolution intended to limit President Trump's ability to conduct further military action in Iran, with only a few senators crossing party lines.

President Trump launched a surprise military strike against Iran, targeting its leadership and military infrastructure without explicit congressional authorization, escalating the conflict with significant casualties including over 1,000 Iranian civilians and six US service members.
center: On Wednesday, the U.S. Senate prepared to vote on a war powers resolution after President Donald Trump launched strikes against Iran, forcing senators to take sides.

Facing an authorization gap, lawmakers pushed the war powers resolution after Trump entered a five-day-old war without prior approval, with Sen. Tim Kaine warning `Nobody gets to hide and give the president an easy pass or an end-run around the Constitution`.

Casualty reports include six U.S. service members killed over the weekend and at least 90 civilians in Iran by Wednesday, with the war potentially lasting eight weeks, said Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.
The Senate defeated a discharge motion 52-6, blocking debate, while House leaders are preparing for a Thursday vote, signaling opposition.
The resolution faces an uphill climb and an expected veto, with lawmakers' votes serving as markers ahead of midterm elections as U.S. troops `remain in harm's way`.
right: The U.S. Senate voted 47 to 53 against a War Powers resolution aimed at halting President Trump's military operations in Iran, led by Senators Kaine, Schumer, and Schiff.
The resolution sought to require congressional approval for further military actions in Iran, citing concerns over constitutional norms.
The vote largely split along party lines, with most Republicans opposing the resolution and defending Trump's actions as necessary against Iranian threats.
The conflict has caused casualties, including six U.S. troops killed in a drone strike, and raised concerns over regional instability and differing views on the conflict's duration and goals.
